plant.cvs: 'Adolphe Audusson' – blood-red semi-double, earlier · 'Bob Hope' – very dark red · 'Nobilissima' – white peony form, very early · 'Elegans' – pink anemone form
plant.foliage: evergreen; glossy, leathery dark green oval leaves
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, even in a cold winter, approximately -15 to -10°C; frost can brown open flowers.
plant.pollination: not applicable; grown for flowers, not fruit
plant.prune: Little needed. Shape lightly straight after flowering, before new buds set.
plant.resilience: Tough, long-lived evergreen in shade. Avoid east facings, where early sun on frosted flowers browns them. Pests: scale insects, vine weevil, occasional aphids.
plant.soilWarning: Lime or chalk causes yellow leaves
sources: General RHS guidance on Camellia japonica, as remembered and not checked online.
General horticultural knowledge of camellia cultivation and pests in the UK.
Cultivar description of 'Blood of China', from memory and not verified.
uncertain: hardiness: H5 is the usual RHS rating for Camellia japonica cultivars, but the band for 'Blood of China' itself was not confirmed.
height and spread: typical RHS ultimate sizes for C. japonica, not confirmed for this cultivar.
peak: remembered as a late-season cultivar. Flowering could run Feb-May depending on region and year.
visual and hue: the flower colour (deep salmon-red) and form (semi-double to loose peony) are from memory and need checking.
clay: left blank. Camellias can grow in acid, moisture-retentive clay that does not waterlog, but tolerance of typical UK clay was not established.
sunMin: an estimate of how much shade it tolerates while still flowering well.
compliance: no plant breeders' rights are expected, because it is an old (c.1920s) American cultivar. No Schedule 9 or biosecurity issue is known. Not checked online.
ratings (pestRisk, thirst, careLevel, growthSpeed, sunNeed) are judged from the general habits of Camellia japonica.
plant.uses: Shady borders · woodland gardens · containers · north or west walls · winter structure
plant.visual: Deep salmon-red double flowers with yellow stamens, late season · glossy dark green evergreen leaves all year
plant.water: Keep evenly moist, especially July to September while buds form; use rainwater in pots. Dry spells cause bud drop.

warnings: "water" and "soil" share the word(s) moist; drainage belongs in one field, not both
